Iochand (A80)

Scoring-table region: Wescann / Gerudia.

In a sentence: Restore an old kingdom shared by a gnomish dynasty and humans, then weave the Dragon Coast's artificery, cultural integration, and overseas subjects into a new maritime polity.

Story: High | Mission tree: Long (43 direct missions) | Mission-tree update: exact date unconfirmed; local version v1.37.5.0 | Distinctiveness: Very high | Tedium: Medium-high | Early pressure: Depends on predecessor | Expansion: High

Lose the kingdom before restoring it

There is no Iochand available to select on the 1444 map. The current A80 country file is a post-formation template: monarchy, Iochander culture, accepted Creek Gnomes, Court of Masks faith, and a Dragon Coast capital. An eligible Creek Gnome or Iochander-culture country that owns the required core provinces can restore it by decision. Portnamm and Southroy are common, but not the only, routes. Southroy also receives a special flag on formation, so the predecessors do not all become identical. [Local scripts]

The offline English Wiki's history gives this restoration goal its weight. After the Dragonwake, the old gnomish state collapsed. In 471, the Creek Gnome Fizwick founded the Kingdom of Iochand around Portnamm, but its population was not exclusively gnomish: Iochander humans, Creek Gnomes, and halflings lived together there. The royal house allied with and became subject to the High Kingdom of Lencenor, endured several wars, and was finally defeated by Reveria in 1264. In a 1444-start campaign, restoring A80 revives a kingdom that had fallen; it does not continue a polity still present in the historical timeline. [Wiki]

That past also shapes the country's identity: Iochand is not simply a story of gnomes conquering humans. The old kingdom began amid disaster and refugee settlement, with a gnomish dynasty ruling alongside human local nobility. Its mission-tree future asks again how the crown, ports, kobolds, and both sides of the strait will coexist. A modern formable can inherit this legacy without automatically inheriting answers to all its political questions. [Wiki] [Local scripts]

The story begins after restoration

The formation decision requires peace, an eligible culture, and five key core provinces; it changes the Tag to A80 and replaces the missions. The 43 direct missions begin with the kingdom's identity, nobility, and gnomish monarchy: events can establish a distinctive royal system, so formation is more than recolouring the map. Gnome, human, and kobold relations on the Dragon Coast then become matters of administration. Some missions address subjects, cultural change, and tolerance. These developments are conditional and involve choices; they do not justify describing every people as equal from the outset or as inevitably forced to assimilate. [Local scripts]

The distinctive midgame is artificery and agricultural experimentation. Missions involving cultivated animals, turning wool into cloth, and paper-making make economic development more than port trade: they give it the character of gnomish craft and laboratory work. This sets Iochand apart from a conventional restoration tree of claims and conquest; engineering, improvement, and production are part of the expansion story. [Local scripts]

The later missions turn toward North Aelantir. Colonies can become a particular A19 subject and develop into a special subject system. As the overseas kingdom grows, events bring tensions around loyalty, tribute, Lencenor, and gnomish hierarchy. The overseas realm is not simply a string of consequence-free colonial rewards: relations between the centre and its subjects can become a crisis for the state. Specific triggers and outcomes are conditional, not a single ending that every predecessor will reach. [Local scripts]

Player experience and personality

Early on, choose which eligible predecessor will restore the kingdom; in midgame, manage a multi-ethnic Dragon Coast and artificery industry; only later do colonisation, subjects, and imperial order take centre stage. A 2023 player post discusses the Portnamm route, while a 2026 experience post praises the Southroy entry and event writing. These can indicate what players enjoy, but cannot establish current mission values. No official developer diary directly explaining A80's current mission tree was found; a diary about a neighbouring region should not be presented as country-specific evidence. [Community views]

The v2.1 personality profile is Expansion 79/100 | Autocracy 67/100 | Magic ↔ Artifice 16/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 89/100) | Pluralism 74/100.

The v2.1 values profile is Neutral (66/100), with a branch-dependent trajectory.

Recommended for players who enjoy a long formable campaign, an artificery economy, and development on both land and sea. If you dislike subject management, colonial events, and multi-ethnic politics, the late game may become more involved than expected. See the evidence page for sourcing and historical limits.

National Ideas

The following reproduces the current local national-idea text and script effects. Traditions apply when the set is adopted; the seven ideas unlock in sequence as points are invested, and the ambition applies after all seven are unlocked. Only national ideas are listed: racial, government and mission bonuses are excluded. A successor idea set does not automatically stack with the earlier set. Idea descriptions may recall history or express future aspirations; they do not automatically establish events already completed in 1444. Names and complete descriptions use the current Mod’s English localisation. Alternative and predecessor/successor sets remain separately conditional, including whether new ideas are accepted on formation.

Effect display units inherited from the source data are reproduced for parity, not revalidated here. Suspicious percentages and script-valued effects require separate review; raw values are shown below.

Iochander Traditions

  • Years of separatism: -5 (years_of_nationalism; raw value -5).

  • Diplomatic relations: +1 (diplomatic_upkeep; raw value 1).

1. The Iochanders

Fair Iochand has teemed with humans from time immemorial, yet its stewards, since even before great Castanor, or the Damerian Republic, have been the Creek Gnomes. The passage of centuries has seen the neighbouring Lencori tribes grow, under our influence, into a unique and beautiful culture, a synthesis of the ways of our peoples. Our language finds its way into their speech, and they flock to our theatres for comedy and drama alike. Most significantly, they have embraced our fashion: the mark of a true Iochander is their red cap, worn with pride, just like their rulers.

  • global_autonomy: -0.05% (global_autonomy; raw value -0.05).

2. The Portroy Creek

The noble Portroy flows through the heart of Iochand, and its waters sustain the realm. Beyond demarcating the boundary between the demesne of the King in the north and that of the Duke in the south, it carries the trade of Portnamm and Turnwell, the twin hubs of commerce in the realm. To the east lies the Small Country, and beyond the Westcoast. The rebirth of Aelantir brings the promise of exotic goods from afar, and they must flow through us.

  • Trade efficiency: +10% (trade_efficiency; raw value 0.1).

  • Ship trade power: +10% (global_ship_trade_power; raw value 0.1).

3. The Gelpalaasd

Since its construction, the beautiful Gelpalaasd, or Yellow Palace, has gleamed as the crown jewel of Iochand. Designed by brilliant Gnomish architects and constructed by their diligent Iochander crews, the palace stands as a monument to the people of the realm, surrounded on all sides by the yellow flowers for which it is named. Dignitaries and nobles from near and far speak of the extravagant balls of the Gelpalaasd, kaleidoscopic affairs of entertainment and decadence, ensconced in the yellow fabric of the palace decor.

  • Diplomatic reputation: +200% (diplomatic_reputation; raw value 2).

4. The Sildthol Seven

The reavers showed no mercy upon their arrival in Cannor, and Iochand suffered the same fate as many realms. Before long, the savage northmen had crushed many of the forces the kingdom could muster, and the people would not rise to aid the realm. The great thinkers and strategists of the royal court toiled fruitlessly over impossible plans to rebuild the army, until insight suddenly struck in an unexpected place. The court jester suggested something more familiar to the people, a simple comedic stage play, to be shown all across the kingdom. The Sildthol Seven follows the story of a ragtag band of Iochanders, three gnomes and three humans, led by the halfling captain Arnol Bravefoot. Stationed in a backwater outpost in the County of Sildthol, they are first to discover a company of reavers, intending a surprise attack while the King's army fought in the north. Stuck between a reaver and a hard place, they wage a campaign of guerilla warfare with tricks, traps, and illusion, leveraging their wits against the bumbling and brutish northmen. The production was a runaway success, and countless Iochanders enlisted in the King's army, energised by new dreams of fun and glory. The popularity of the play did not fade over time, and has been adapted to every medium from bard song to bedtime story, inspiring each new generation to defend Iochand.

  • Manpower recovery speed: +15% (manpower_recovery_speed; raw value 0.15).

5. University of Portnamm

The devastation of the Dragonwake destroyed all but two branches of the Gommo, one on the isle of Nimscodd, and the other in Portnamm, the oldest and most important city of the kingdom. The Gommo branch retained its independence from the crown, and the passage of centuries saw it grow into the University of Portnamm, expanding from artificery alone to include a broader curriculum born of the culture of our people. Actors and authors come from far and wide to learn the dramatic arts, and behind the curtain stagehands study the science of pyrotechnics and stage effects, pushing Iochander theatre to new heights of creativity. In the countryside's idyllic fields, scholars experiment with dazzling new innovations of artificery, ever striving to further augment Iochand's agricultural output and keep the kingdom on the cutting edge.

  • Technology cost: -5% (technology_cost; raw value -0.05).

6. The Royal Jester of Iochand

The jesters of the realms of Cannor enjoy the "Jester's Privilege," granting them the right to speak freely, and even mock their ruler. Iochander's masked Royal Jester, the Naar, remains a position of great prestige within the court, but it is not entertainment alone the sovereigns seek. The Royal Jester's mask remains the same, but with each encounter, the voice changes, the mannerisms shift, and courtiers are never sure of whether the figure with whom they were speaking was a different act, or a different jester. Both have been true at different times, for the Royal Jester’s greatest role is that of the spymaster of Iochand, overseeing a network of spies harvested from the capable ranks of the kingdom's many troupes of actors.

  • Spy network construction: +20% (spy_offence; raw value 0.2).

  • global_spy_defence: +20% (global_spy_defence; raw value 0.2).

7. The Greencap Elite

The red cap of the gnome, ever present throughout recorded history, is popular with the Iochander Lencori to the extent that it became part of our military uniform, and the sight of our ranks of red capped soldiers, heights varying wildly, identifies our regiments at a glance. While the kingdom's boorish foes may mock our timeless Gnomish fashion, the appearance of a green-capped soldier chills them to the bone. The gallant Greencaps, a company of elite warriors, armed to the teeth, and drilled into a lethal machine, stand as leaders amongst the rank and file, using their experience to outwit and outlast the enemies of Iochand, and striking fear into all who oppose them. But then again, not everything in Iochand is based on a true story. The Greencaps are not an elite order, or even a formal component of the army. In truth, the green caps are given to soldiers with experience in the performing arts, and rotate through the regiments, the wearer tasked with the honour of entertaining their comrades by telling tales of past glory, improvising ruthless mockery of their foes, and staying their hearts with songs of hope. The reputation of the green cap is no secret to its wearers, and they take pride in maintaining the great deception, in hopes that the doubts of the enemy may become opportunities for clever tactics, leaving them as clueless as they are defeated.

  • Army morale: +15% (land_morale; raw value 0.15).
